headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger’s test is generally not recommended when fewer than 10 studies are available.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 2 studies yielded an effect size of 0.63 (95% CI: 0.39–1.01), indicating no statistically significant association between tea and kidney and renal pelvis cancer. Although the point estimate suggests a potential inverse relationship, the confidence interval includes the null. These findings were accompanied by moderate heterogeneity (I² = 38.87%), suggesting some variability in the results across studies.
